items.title: Manuel Mello Interview, 1959-08-03
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] And this is Richard Allen. Manny J. Mello. We're recording this afternoon... [INTERVIEWEE] Manny J. Mello. That's what they always did call me.

ctx.x: You know, I noticed you mentioned a lot of Germans with Steckler by name that they sound like... It was all Germans.

It was all Germans. Baptiste is the only Frenchman. His name is Jean-Baptiste Steckler. And I used to laugh, my daughter. He was a case. He still is a case. Yeah, I learned down at Holy Cross College. And when I started playing with what we call a GDNC band, that is four pieces or five pieces, they could play and I couldn't because I could read and they could and I couldn't fake. They could fake what I couldn't read. Boy, was a dag-gun this time trying to get next to that, but it didn't take long. It didn't take…
Which was your very first job playing music professionally? Professionally?

items.title: Manuel Mello Interview, 1959-08-03
items.q: Who is that, Alan? Nigga Allen from Dretton.

ctx.x: Colored that was with a beating heart with a colored folks. They used to have a dance every Saturday night. L-I-V-A had to get all that stuff because L-I-V-A had to have to hit a piece twice or three times before I could play it. But then L-I-V-A had to hit that thing once. Lance, Lance, he'd hit that thing once. Boy, he might make one or two humbugs on it, but he ain't gonna make too many humbugs. He had a quick ear and a good ear. I mean a real good ear. Did you tell me one time that he used to go around to…
Did Lyle's work with many bands that you didn't work with? Well,
